scenes.text: Three Claude models get the same brief and the same critic. Which beach house would you keep?
scenes.say: Three Claude models get the same brief, the same tools and the same critic. Each builds a beach house. Which one would you keep?

scenes.headline: Opus, Fable and Sonnet build the same beach house
scenes.sub: A critic loop, a baked light, and a blind judgement
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Dormer! Today, three beach houses built from one brief, and what each one cost.

scenes.title: One brief, one loop
scenes.sub: Build, bake, screenshot, ask a stranger
scenes.say: Chapter one. One brief, one loop.

scenes.text: Bake the light once, offline, into texture atlases, so the browser draws every surface unlit.
scenes.term: Atlas: one texture holding every surface's light
scenes.say: A browser can't trace soft sunlight through a balustrade. So the light is computed once in Blender and pasted onto every surface as a texture.

steps.say: A Python script builds the whole house from nothing. No downloaded models, textures or skies. Then Cycles bakes the light.
The geometry and atlases are packed into one file of about five megabytes, and headless Chrome screenshots it in this site's own viewer.

steps.term: Critic: a subagent that has seen nothing else
steps.say: Then a brand new subagent gets the brief and the pictures, never the code, and answers yes or no, with at most five ranked fixes.

steps.note: repeat until a critic says yes
steps.say: Fix the worst thing first, and go again, until a critic says yes.

scenes.title: One pass, as Sonnet 5.5 ran it

steps.say: Sonnet wrote its own geometry library, so the house is about four thousand flat faces before Blender ever sees it.

steps.term: Samples: rays per texel in the bake
steps.say: Cycles bakes two passes per face, colour at eight samples and light at four hundred, and the script multiplies them.
The file came out over budget, so it turned the JPEG quality down instead of baking again.
And on the third round, the critic said yes.

scenes.title: Three ways to build it
scenes.say: Chapter two. Three ways to build it.

steps.say: Opus baked colour and light together, ran seven passes, and dressed the site best: a dune fence, a fire pit, a stepped boardwalk.
It also repainted the siding blue grey on its own. Four critics, and not one yes.

steps.term: Light-only bake: colour is painted on afterwards
steps.say: Fable never asked Cycles for colour. It baked only light, denoised it hard, and painted boards and tiles on afterwards in Python.
So the rail shadows on this balcony stay sharp. It needed five rounds, and its last four baked on a CPU.
Sonnet's house is the crispest and the smallest file. Clean lines, black framed sliders, the biggest glazing of the three.
But the furniture is plain boxes, and the rooms are thin.

scenes.title: The race, and the verdicts
scenes.sub: Who got a yes, and who won
scenes.say: Chapter three. The race, and the verdicts.

judged: first for two of three judges

steps.say: Here are the three loops on one clock, from launch to the finished file. Each dot is a critic's verdict.
Sonnet. No, no, then yes, in about forty two minutes. The fastest yes on the page.
Opus. Four critics, four noes, the last one close, at about forty eight minutes. It never got a yes.
Fable. Three noes, then two yeses in a row, at about ninety three minutes, across two days and three machines.
Then three blind judges ranked matched views of all three. The cheapest yes came last with every one of them.

scenes.title: First places, 33 blind view judgements
scenes.note: three judges, eleven matched views each
scenes.say: Across thirty three view judgements, Fable took seventeen first places and Opus sixteen. Opus won every aerial. Fable won the deck, the balcony and the bathroom with every judge.

scenes.title: What the judgement cannot tell you

items.text: The judges are Claude models too
items.say: The judges are Claude models judging Claude models, one pinned to each.
I placed the cameras by one rule, but the floor plans differ, so the spots are my call.
And three judges looked at still frames. Nobody walked the houses for the ranking.

scenes.text: A critic's yes means nothing is visibly broken. It does not mean the house is good.
scenes.say: So remember: a critic's yes means nothing is visibly broken. It does not mean the house is good. Rounds are what you pay for.

recap: Bake the light, draw it unlit
Fable first, Opus best from the air
scenes.say: Bake the light and draw it unlit. Sonnet got the fastest yes and came last. Fable won narrowly, and Opus is best from the air. Thanks for watching!
